Keep profiles in a main-process allowlist, move HTTP and authenticated SSE into Electron, preserve reconnect behavior, and surface completion notifications when the window is backgrounded. Add regression coverage, packaging CI, and operator documentation so unsigned artifacts can be built and tested consistently.

+### Electron and Windows packaging
+
+- **Electron 43** owns main-process HTTP and SSE connections. Renderer receives only frozen preload
+  methods; `contextIsolation`, sandbox, and disabled Node integration are load-bearing.
+- **electron-builder 26** creates unsigned x64 Windows NSIS artifacts. No signing secret is configured;
+  SmartScreen warnings are expected. `web/release/` is generated and must not be committed.
+- Renderer `web/dist` is built with Vite `--base=./` for `file://` loading. Standard `npm run build`
+  keeps PWA/Pages absolute-base behavior.
+- `electron-icon.svg` is separate from Android/PWA icon assets. Do not change native platform icons
+  when adjusting Windows branding.
+- Saved profiles are validated and persisted by main process under Electron `userData`; request and
+  stream calls carry profile IDs plus relative operations, never complete target URLs.

commits.author: Giulio Ardoino
commits.subject: fix(desktop): survive window teardown and non-Windows platforms
commits.body:
Closing the window raised "A JavaScript error occurred in the main process:
TypeError: Object has been destroyed". The `closed` event fires after the
native window is gone, so reading window.webContents from inside it throws;
the reference is now taken once at creation and reused.

The debounced window-state save had the same exposure from the other side: a
resize or move during teardown could schedule a write that fired after the
window was destroyed. The pending timer is cancelled on close now, and the
save itself bails on a destroyed window.

Guard the platform-specific main-process calls while here, so the shell holds
up outside Windows:

- setOverlayIcon is absent on macOS and Linux rather than inert, so an
  unguarded call throws out of the focus handler.
- macOS keeps its application menu, which is where Cmd+Q and the Edit menu's
  clipboard shortcuts come from, and no longer quits when its last window
  closes: reopening from the dock is what "activate" is for.
- The overlay badge reads the PNG app icon, since nativeImage cannot decode
  SVG and was handed an empty image every time.

commits.author: Giulio Ardoino
commits.subject: fix(web): let the desktop layout fill the window
commits.body:
The desktop shell hugged the combined width of two fixed panels, so on any
display wider than about 1160px the whole app sat in a column in the middle
with dead space either side, and the only way to use the rest of the window
was to drag the panel borders outwards by hand.

The sidebar keeps its resizable width; the main pane flexes into whatever is
left. That leaves one border worth dragging — the divider between the two —
so the sidebar's outer edge and the pane's right edge, which are now the
window's own edges, no longer carry handles. The main pane needs no stored
width of its own any more.

The transcript and composer share a centred column capped at 80rem instead of
stretching with the pane: filling the window should not mean running prose out
to 2000px. The chat jump buttons follow that column's edge rather than the
pane's, so they stay beside the conversation.

commits.author: Giulio Ardoino
commits.subject: ci: build macOS and Linux desktop apps alongside Windows
commits.body:
Every v* tag published an Android APK and a Windows installer; macOS and Linux
users had nothing to download. electron-builder cannot cross-compile, so each
artifact has to be built on its own runner: the Windows-only workflow becomes
one matrix over windows-latest, macos-latest and ubuntu-latest, and the release
job attaches everything it produced to the tag's release.

- macOS: dmg and zip for arm64 and x64. Nothing is signed, so signing identity
  discovery is switched off explicitly — left on, electron-builder hunts for an
  identity in the runner keychain and fails the build when it finds none.
- Linux: AppImage and deb, x64.
- mac and linux artifacts are collected by extension rather than by
  artifactName, because electron-builder normalises some filenames (deb in
  particular) and if-no-files-found would then fail a build that succeeded.
- fail-fast is off: one desktop breaking should still leave the others
  attachable.

All three targets take their icon from the 1024px PWA app icon, so the SVG
added for Windows alone goes; nativeImage could not read it anyway. The Android
workflow owns release creation and its notes said "Android release APK", which
is no longer the whole story.

@@ -0,0 +1,144 @@
+name: Build desktop apps
+
+"on":
+  workflow_dispatch: {}
+  push:
+    branches: [main]
+    tags: ['v*']
+    paths:
+      - 'web/src/**'
+      - 'web/electron/**'
+      - 'web/public/**'
+      - 'web/index.html'
+      - 'web/package.json'
+      - 'web/package-lock.json'
+      - 'web/tsconfig*.json'
+      - 'web/vite.config.ts'
+      - '.github/workflows/desktop-apps.yml'
+      - 'bridge/**'
+
+permissions:
+  contents: read
+
+jobs:
+  package:
+    name: Package ${{ matrix.platform }}
+    runs-on: ${{ matrix.os }}
+    strategy:
+      # One desktop failing should still leave the other two attachable to the release.
+      fail-fast: false
+      matrix:
+        include:
+          - platform: windows
+            os: windows-latest
+            script: package:win
+            artifacts: |
+              web/release/Harness-Remote-*-win-x64-unsigned.exe
+          # Matched by extension rather than by artifactName: electron-builder normalises the
+          # filename for some targets (deb in particular), and if-no-files-found: error would then
+          # fail a build that actually succeeded. release/ holds nothing but build output.
+          - platform: macos
+            os: macos-latest
+            script: package:mac
+            artifacts: |
+              web/release/*.dmg
+              web/release/*.zip
+          - platform: linux
+            os: ubuntu-latest
+            script: package:linux
+            artifacts: |
+              web/release/*.AppImage
+              web/release/*.deb
+    steps:
+      - name: Checkout
+        uses: actions/checkout@v7
+
+      - name: Setup Node.js
+        uses: actions/setup-node@v7
+        with:
+          node-version: 22
+          cache: npm
+          cache-dependency-path: web/package-lock.json
+
+      - name: Install web dependencies
+        run: npm ci
+        working-directory: web
+
+      - name: Build PWA renderer
+        run: npm run build
+        working-directory: web
+
+      - name: Run web regression tests
+        run: |
+          npm run test:i18n
+          npm run test:config
+          npm run test:ui
+          npm run test:settings
+          npm run test:platform
+          npm run test:model
+          npm run test:events
+          npm run test:profiles
+          npm run test:desktop
+        working-directory: web
+
+      - name: Run bridge tests
+        run: npm test
+        working-directory: bridge
+
+      - name: Build unsigned ${{ matrix.platform }} artifacts
+        run: npm run ${{ matrix.script }}
+        working-directory: web
+        env:
+          # Nothing here is signed. Left on, electron-builder goes looking for a macOS identity in
+          # the runner's keychain and fails the build when it does not find one.
+          CSC_IDENTITY_AUTO_DISCOVERY: false
+
+      - name: Upload ${{ matrix.platform }} artifacts
+        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v7
+        with:
+          name: harness-remote-desktop-${{ matrix.platform }}-${{ github.sha }}
+          path: ${{ matrix.artifacts }}
+          if-no-files-found: error
+
+  release:
+    if: startsWith(github.ref, 'refs/tags/v')
+    needs: package
+    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
+    permissions:
+      contents: write
+    steps:
+      - name: Download desktop artifacts
+        uses: actions/download-artifact@v8
+        with:
+          pattern: harness-remote-desktop-*-${{ github.sha }}
+          merge-multiple: true
+          path: release
+
+      - name: Wait for Android-owned release
+        env:
+          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
+          TAG: ${{ github.ref_name }}
+          REPO: ${{ github.repository }}
+        run: |
+          deadline=$(( $(date +%s) + 600 ))
+          until gh release view "$TAG" --repo "$REPO" >/dev/null 2>&1; do
+            if [ "$(date +%s)" -ge "$deadline" ]; then
+              echo "GitHub release $TAG did not appear within 10 minutes; the Android workflow publishes it first." >&2
+              exit 1
+            fi
+            sleep 10
+          done
+
+      - name: Attach desktop artifacts to release
+        env:
+          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
+          TAG: ${{ github.ref_name }}
+        run: |
+          shopt -s nullglob
+          files=(release/*)
+          if [ ${#files[@]} -eq 0 ]; then
+            echo "No desktop artifacts were downloaded." >&2
+            exit 1
+          fi
+          printf 'attaching %s\n' "${files[@]}"
+          gh release upload "$TAG" "${files[@]}" --clobber
